author: constitution state news
title: Andy Shay named NEILA Coach of the Year as five Yale players earn honors
text:
Yale men’s lacrosse head coach Andy Shay was named Coach of the Year by the New England Intercollegiate Lacrosse Association, and five team members received All-New England honors, according to a May 20 announcement.
The recognition follows a season in which Yale returned to the NCAA Tournament for the first time since 2023. The Bulldogs’ roster included 13 first-year players. After starting with three wins and four losses overall and no league victories, Yale won six out of its next seven games. These included wins over No. 9 Cornell, No. 5 Harvard, and No. 18 Boston University, helping establish Yale as a postseason contender.
Shay led his team into the NCAA Tournament First Round against Syracuse. The Bulldogs narrowly lost that game by one goal after Syracuse’s goalkeeper made several saves in the final seconds.
Five Yale players were recognized by NEILA: Connor Gately and Patrick Pisano were selected for the first team; Cole Cashion, Peter Moynihan, and Konrad Miklaszewski earned second-team honors. Gately led Yale with 32 assists and 57 points this season while scoring at least two assists in eleven games. Pisano earned All-America accolades from Inside Lacrosse and USA Lacrosse Magazine; he led Yale with 22 caused turnovers this year.
Cashion scored in eight straight games during his junior season and finished tied for third on the team with twenty goals. Moynihan also tallied twenty goals this year—including four game-winning scores—and contributed key performances against Cornell and Brown late in the season. Miklaszewski played fourteen games as part of Yale’s defense, collecting sixteen ground balls.
Looking ahead, these individual achievements highlight both player development within the program and potential for future seasons under Shay’s leadership.
